questions.text: What is the primary operational mode of your AI systems?

options.text: Drafting and recommendation with mandatory human review before any action.
Automated workflow routing, data classification, and internal summarization.
Autonomous agents with API access capable of executing transactions or modifying state.

questions.text: How do your AI agents authenticate to internal databases or external services?

options.text: They don't. All data is provided explicitly by the user in the prompt.
They use a static, ambient service account with broad read permissions.
They use dynamic, user-delegated tokens to perform actions on behalf of a specific human.

questions.text: If an AI model generates an incorrect decision, what is the maximum potential business impact?

options.text: Low. A human catches the error before any external release.
Moderate. Internal delays or minor reputational friction.
Severe. Financial loss, regulatory fines, or critical infrastructure failure.

questions.text: What type of data is routinely processed by your AI models?

options.text: Public or non-sensitive corporate knowledge base data.
Internal confidential IP, proprietary code, or strategic memos.
Highly regulated PII, PHI, financial records, or strict NDAs.

questions.text: How are you currently managing 'Shadow AI' (unmanaged employee use of public models)?

options.text: We rely on an acceptable use policy and employee trust.
We use basic network blocklists to prevent access to known consumer AI tools.
We lack visibility, but suspect sensitive data is leaking through browser-based AI chats.

questions.text: Can you programmatically prove that a specific data payload was NOT sent to a third-party LLM?

options.text: Yes, we don't use third-party LLMs.
No, we have to search application logs which may be incomplete.
No, and this is a major concern for our GDPR/CCPA compliance.

questions.text: What is the primary driver for AI governance in your organization?

options.text: Internal alignment, best practices, and innovation safety.
Customer procurement requirements (e.g., SOC2, ISO 42001).
Strict regulatory mandates (EU AI Act, HIPAA) or high liability environments.

questions.text: How do you currently evidence AI policy compliance during an audit?

options.text: Manual review of static PDF policies, risk registers, and approval emails.
Review of standard SIEM application logs and MLOps dashboards.
We currently have no reliable mechanism to prove runtime compliance.

questions.text: If your AI-generated content is disputed in a legal setting, how do you prove its origin?

options.text: We don't publish AI-generated content externally.
We rely on metadata tags or visible watermarks (which can be stripped).
We lack cryptographic provenance or forensic fingerprinting for our outputs.

profiles.title: Profile 1: Internal Evidence
profiles.description: Your AI deployment is primarily low-risk and internally focused. Your governance priority is establishing basic visibility and policy alignment without heavy overhead.
actionItems: Implement basic telemetry to monitor for 'Shadow AI' usage.
Ensure human-in-the-loop review for all generative outputs.

profiles.title: Profile 2: Regulated Evidence
profiles.description: You are processing sensitive data or subject to B2B compliance audits. You require structured evidence that your AI systems are adhering to defined security boundaries.
actionItems: Translate PDF policies into machine-evaluable gates.
Implement a Tamper-Evident Evidence Vault for AI logs.
Begin mapping systems to ISO 42001 or the EU AI Act.

profiles.title: Profile 3: Forensic Evidence
profiles.description: You are deploying high-stakes, autonomous agents or operating in strictly regulated environments. You require mathematically provable, cryptographic assurance for every AI action.
actionItems: Implement Pre-Action Proof-Carrying Tool Execution for all agents.
Deploy Lazy Capsule Materialization (LCM) for audit-ready compliance.
Establish Dual-State Hashing pipelines for downstream artifact defensibility.
